summary: Secondary JS SDK packages — React renderers, scaffolder CLI, codegen tooling, and reserved-but-deferred stubs (groq, nextjs-query) — that extend the core Barkpark client into framework-specific developer surfaces. Together they form the consumer-facing JS distribution layer.

intentions.title: Ship a complete, framework-aware JS SDK for Barkpark consumers
intentions.evidence: react/tsup.config.ts builds dual CJS+ESM with a server entry and auto-injected 'use client' banner; codegen/tsup.config.ts builds a CLI+library for typed-client generation; create-barkpark-app/tsup.config.ts produces a Node scaffolder — together they cover the full DX lifecycle (scaffold → typed client → render)

intentions.title: Enforce React Server Component boundaries at build time
intentions.evidence: react/tsup.config.ts prependUseClient() only on client bundle entries (index.mjs/cjs) while keeping server.ts directive-free, ensuring Next.js App Router can tree-shake correctly without manual annotation

intentions.title: Reserve roadmap surface without shipping broken code
intentions.evidence: groq/src/index.ts and nextjs-query/src/index.ts both throw eagerly at import time with a roadmap URL — prevents accidental 1.0 shipping against empty packages while holding the npm names for 1.1

intentions.title: Keep bundle size a first-class constraint
intentions.evidence: Both react and codegen configs enable treeshake:true and splitting:true; codegen marks heavy deps (chokidar, cac, zod, prettier) as external; react marks react/react-dom/@barkpark/core external — minimising what ships to end-user bundles

intentions.title: Provide a zero-config project scaffolder
intentions.evidence: create-barkpark-app/tsup.config.ts produces a shebang-bannered ESM-only Node 20 binary with version constant baked in, ready for npx consumption without install
